title: Observation of electron spin interactions between Rydberg atoms
authors: Le Ruan, Ziqi Zhou, Yuchen Guo, Chengshu Li, Cheng Chen
abstract: We report the observation of electron spin interactions between Rydberg atoms, which are driven by spin-orbit coupling through second-order dipole perturbation and exhibit a spatial anisotropy governed by the atomic configuration. Specifically, we observe coherent electron spin exchange dynamics, with the measured coupling strength agreeing well with both numerical calculations and theoretical models. Furthermore, we show that global microwave dressing enables active engineering and dynamical freezing of the spin exchange by introducing a differential AC Stark shift between the participating states. Additionally, we achieve tunability of the interaction by applying a stronger magnetic field, which effectively modifies the energy contributions of the underlying spin-orbit coupling channels. Finally, measuring spin dynamics in one-dimensional multi-atom chains aligned parallel or perpendicular to the magnetic field provides a self-consistent validation of the anisotropic XXZ framework. This electron spin interaction natively features spin-position coupling and enables a natural mapping onto the Heisenberg-Kitaev model. Our findings reveal a new class of electron spin-spin interactions among Rydberg atoms, expanding the scope of quantum simulation with Rydberg atom arrays.
summary: The researchers report the observation of electron spin interactions between Rydberg atoms, showing these interactions are driven by spin-orbit coupling and follow an anisotropic XXZ model. They demonstrate active control over this interaction using microwave dressing and magnetic fields. Crucially, they distinguish this genuine spin exchange from orbital exchange by measuring a pronounced angular anisotropy unique to the spin-exchange channel.
main_problem: The study aims to observe and characterize the electron spin interactions between Rydberg atoms, specifically distinguishing this genuine spin exchange from purely orbital exchange mechanisms.
main_result: The authors successfully observed coherent electron spin exchange dynamics governed by an anisotropic XXZ model, and crucially, they distinguished this spin interaction from orbital exchange by measuring a strong angular dependence in the spin-exchange coupling.
method: The research employs controlled Rydberg atom arrays, utilizing microwave dressing and magnetic field tuning to manipulate and measure the spin-exchange dynamics between atoms.
model_or_system: The system involves Rydberg atoms (e.g., Rb) where spin qubits are encoded in Zeeman sublevels. The interaction is modeled by an anisotropic XXZ Hamiltonian, $H = \sum_{i<j} [J_{xy}(	heta_{ij})(S_x^i S_x^j + S_y^i S_y^j) + J_z(	heta_{ij})S_z^i S_z^j]$, which arises from spin-orbit coupling via second-order dipole perturbation.
key_observables: Coherent electron spin exchange dynamics, coupling strengths ($J_{xy}, J_z$), and the angular dependence of the exchange coupling $J_{xy}(	heta) \propto (5 + 3 \cos 2	heta)/8$.
important_parameters: Interatomic separation ($d = 9.66 \mu	ext{m}$), magnetic field strength (up to $51.5 	ext{ G}$), and the angle $	heta$ defining the relative orientation of the atoms.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on second-order dipole perturbation theory to derive the spin-orbit coupling mechanism, and the fidelity of the measurement is corrected for various experimental imperfections (SPAM errors).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between spin exchange vs. conventional dipole-dipole exchange, show the time evolution of spin populations under microwave dressing, and demonstrate the contrast between the strongly anisotropic $\Delta n=2$ spin exchange and the nearly isotropic $\Delta n=1$ orbital exchange.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the observation of spin exchange, detailing control mechanisms (dressing, field tuning), quantifying the interaction anisotropy via theoretical mapping to the XXZ model, and finally providing a definitive diagnostic by contrasting the angular dependence of spin exchange ($\Delta n=2$) against orbital exchange ($\Delta n=1$).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a clean, experimentally verified platform for realizing and controlling spin-spin interactions in arrays, directly mapping onto fundamental models like the Heisenberg-Kitaev model, which is a major focus in quantum simulation.
